strengths: The idea of learning low-dimensional representations for viticultural regions and grape varieties to improve the performance of downstream tasks seems novel and interesting.
The paper also conducted experiments to investigate the property of the latent representation space.

This paper applies joint variational autoencoder (VAE) networks to the study of viticultural regions and grape variety, demonstrating that the embeddings in the paper outperform the "raw" features on downstream tasks. This paper examine whether the joint autoencoder network may be used as a varietal suitability ranking system.

I am a big fan of both, representation learning and wine, so I was very excited to read this paper. I am not familiar with prior literature on wine representation learning, but the authors say it is scarce, i.e. this paper is exploring a novel application area.
weaknesses: The writing of the paper could be improved as it is sometimes difficult to follow the paper.
The paper is incremental since it simply applies VAE to learn the latent representations of grape varieties and viticultural regions.

I think the joining loss is quite important in aligning the representations of regions and varieties. The paper introduces three different joining losses. However, the details of these losses are missing from the paper.
The paper lists the weights of different losses in the paper. However, it is unclear how these weights are chosen.
I find the Results & Discussion section difficult to follow. There is no explicit introduction to the datasets, baselines, experimental setups and research questions.

The English of the manuscript must be improved. There are problems with context transition and logical cohesion, and there are errors in the use of proper nouns. The methods and framework employed in the paper exhibit limited originality and innovation.
Section 1.1 extensively discusses the current research status in the field of viticulture, which is less relevant to the research of this paper.
Section 1.2 introduces the development process of embedding in detail, lacking an introduction to related technologies and methods.
The section 1.3 on "REGION AND VARIETY EMBEDDING REQUIREMENTS" is excessively lengthy and lacks emphasis on key points. It occupies an entire page, which is excessive.
The formulas used in this paper are not numbered.
There are errors in the description of variable v_i.
The description of the variables in the formulas is unclear.
Confusing organization of content in the part of the paper that tests the model on downstream tasks.
The description of specific parameter settings in section 2.3 is excessively lengthy. It is recommended to provide these details in APPENDIX.
The authors should compare their methodology with existing approaches, both qualitatively and quantitatively, to demonstrate its advantages or innovations in the field.

The contribution, the authors claim, to overcome the lack of detailed data. But, quantitative comparison of the above argument is hard to find in the discussion about the effectiveness in the experiments. The authors are strongly suggested to show the strength of the article in overcoming the lack of detailed data. In addition, time complexity or computation overhead analyses need be discussed properly.
Novelty is limited on the methodological side since it aims to apply an existing method to tackle an application problem.
No alternative baseline is used; it focuses on feature ablations of the proposed method.
Lack of clarity in writing and presentation.
Unclear motivation for a coupled region-variety representation.
Insufficient and unconvincing evaluation.
Insufficient benchmark comparisons, in particular using simpler non-deep-learning baseline models.
The presentation is very confusing; the introduction does not clearly state the goals, input data, output, and performance metrics.

The whole sampling approach and sampling-based evaluation are not very clear; it is unclear whether each variety or region receives a single embedding vector or a distribution, and whether that distribution can be multimodal.
Many technical details are unclear, such as what K is used for K-means clustering and why, and what the A/B/C classes used for classification are.
The motivation for using coupled VAEs is not clearly explained, leaving uncertainty about how the latent spaces should meaningfully overlap.
Evaluation tables (e.g., Tables 1–5) provide limited insight into the meaningfulness of the representations, with weak results and lack of statistical significance.
Qualitative evaluations are lacking; visualizations of the latent space are only in the Appendix using PCA and appear unintuitive, suggesting the need for alternative visualizations like t‑SNE.
Lack of proper baselines; comparisons are limited to a simple latitude/longitude model instead of using methods that leverage the A_ij matrix such as regression, SVD, or NNMF.
